## A — Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing
The cover identifies this Wyoming driver manual as the 2021 edition [A01].
The Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services Program issues the state's driver licenses [A02].
This dossier covers stopping, lane changes, turns and backing for the noncommercial passenger-car applicant path.
The handbook says its written test draws on the manual and covers sign recognition, signals, markings, driving laws, safety, crash prevention and vehicle equipment [A03].
No unambiguous written-test question count, passing threshold, bank size or time limit has been verified; these official exam fields remain unknown (verify WY-SEC08-EXAM, WY-SEC08-PASS).
The current issuer page links this edition but warns that print-date information may be outdated; effective date and present applicability need confirmation (verify WY-SEC08-FRESH).

sections.heading: B — Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing
sections.markdown:
## B — Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing
Audience: first-time applicants preparing for a Wyoming noncommercial passenger-car written knowledge test, with stopping, lane changes, turns and backing as this section's subject.
Learning level: beginner. The source scope is the mapped physical pages; explanations use original wording and retain every actor and exception.
Passenger-car applicants study emergency yielding, pedestrian stops, braking, school buses, lane changes, turn preparation and backing.
This dossier teaches the handbook source; it does not confer a license, replace required exams or establish current eligibility independently.

## C — Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing
FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
To let an emergency vehicle pass, stop as close as practicable to the roadway's right edge or curb. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Do not stop in an intersection while yielding to an emergency vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has gone past. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Keep a foot on the brake so the emergency-vehicle driver can tell that you have stopped. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Check for additional emergency vehicles before starting to move again. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
When approaching a roundabout, pull over to allow an emergency vehicle to pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
If already circulating in a roundabout, continue to your exit, leave it and then pull right for the emergency vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
Unless police direct otherwise, a driver on a highway with two or more lanes must merge to the farthest lane when approaching a parked authorized emergency, municipal, public-utility, highway-construction or maintenance vehicle displaying flashing lights or visual signals. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
On a road with one lane each way, approaching a parked emergency vehicle requires reducing speed to at least 20 mph below the speed limit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A01
Drivers and pedestrians both share responsibility for traffic safety. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A01
Yield to a pedestrian in a marked crosswalk on your side of the roadway whether traffic signals are present or absent. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A01
When making a lawful red-light turn after a complete stop, yield to pedestrians. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A01
Yield to a blind pedestrian with a clearly visible white cane or a guide dog. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A01
The handbook allows at least one second to identify a hazard, predict events and decide what to do before executing the response. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A01
The handbook estimates about three-quarters of a second to transfer the foot from accelerator to brake. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
Braking distance depends on starting speed, brakes, tires, pavement and weather. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
A tractor-trailer needs more stopping time and distance than a passenger car at the same speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

sections.domain: Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing — C.02
sections.heading: C — Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing
sections.markdown:
## C — Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing
FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A02
The handbook's example at 55 mph gives a passenger vehicle a typical stopping distance of about 130 to 140 feet. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A02
In the comparison, a heavy vehicle with a loaded trailer usually takes about 190 to 200 feet to stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A02
The handbook's heavy-traffic example says hot truck brakes may increase stopping distance to about 400 feet. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A02
Fatigue, alcohol or inattention can prevent timely hazard recognition and slow reaction to the danger. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A02
When meeting or overtaking a stopped school bus with flashing red lights, stop from either direction unless a physical barrier or separate roadway divides you from the bus. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A02
After stopping for the bus, wait until it moves again or its flashing red lights stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A02
Even when physical separation permits passing a red-light school bus, use extreme caution and watch for pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A02
Stop before the crosswalk at a stop sign, a red traffic light or a flashing red light. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A02
Stop when entering a street from a driveway, alley, building or parking lot. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A02
Stop when entering a business district from a side road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A02
Stop when a police officer directs it, because the officer's directions take precedence over signs and lights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A02
Stop for active red lights or crossing gates at a railroad crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A02
Stop when a flag person signals you at or near a railroad crossing or construction site. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A02
Stop for a blind person attempting to cross a street with a white cane or guide dog. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A02
Stop if you are involved in a traffic crash in any way. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A03
The handbook's school-bus layouts include an undivided highway with two or four lanes and a divided roadway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A03
When a school-bus stop is required on a divided roadway, only traffic on the bus's side of the separation must stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

Misconceptions: A divided-road school-bus exception does not apply merely because traffic has several lanes; emergency traffic circulating behind a roundabout driver is handled after exiting.
Mnemonics: Recall index: mirrors, shoulder, other movers, signal; these are the listed lane-change checks.
Glossary: Recall terms: marked crosswalk, physical barrier, blind spot, reaction interval, turn signal and backing.
Dynamic facts: Vehicle stopping performance is illustrative and depends on equipment and conditions. Present legal applicability remains source freshness debt; no installation or contact list is reproduced.

sections.domain: Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing — C2.01
sections.heading: C2 — Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Stopping, lane changes, turns and backing
FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
Before a lane change, check both the rearview and side mirrors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A01
Before changing lanes, look over the appropriate shoulder to check the blind spot. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A01
Check whether another driver is moving toward the same lane before you change lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A01
Signal before moving into another lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A01
The handbook prohibits lane changes before or within an intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A01
A driver must signal a turn or a lane change. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A01
The turn-signaling instruction calls for signaling at least 100 feet from the intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A01
At higher speeds, the handbook recommends signaling at least four to five seconds before the intended turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A01
Electrical signals should indicate the intended direction: right for a right turn and left for a left turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A01
Hand signals should be made with the left arm. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A01
For a right-turn hand signal, extend the hand and forearm straight upward from the elbow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A02
For a slowing or stopping hand signal, extend the hand and arm downward from the elbow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A02
Plan a turn ahead of time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A02
Move into the proper lane well before turning, using the proper lane-change steps. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A02
Signal the direction of the planned turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A02
Slow down and check for people or vehicles in the turning path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A02
Complete the turn into the proper lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A02
After the turn, adjust speed to match traffic flow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A03
Before backing, walk behind the vehicle to check the space. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A03
While backing, do not rely on mirrors alone; turn the head and body to see the backing path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A03
For backing, place a hand at the top of the steering wheel and move slowly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A03
Stay ready to stop throughout a backing maneuver. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]
